paper.title: A-CODE: Fully Atomic Protein Co-Design with Unified Multimodal Diffusion
paper.section: 4.2 Conditional Binder Design Benchmark; Appendix C.2 Binder Design
paper.quote_task: We benchmark the conditional generation ability of A-CODE on a test set comprising 10 protein targets with diverse structural properties, as proposed in Zambaldi et al. In binder design, a target protein with known sequence and structure is fed in as the conditions for the generative model. Hotspot information of the binding site is often available as additional input. For a unified evaluation, we follow PXDesign to use the filter from AF2-IG. For each different target, we sample 328-728 binders with lengths ranging from 80 to 130, following the same protocol in PXDesign, and report the percentage of designable samples as Designability. We evaluate both the model-generated co-designed sequence and the PMPNN-redesigned single sequence as separate variants.
paper.quote_filter: Designability is the major metric used here, where we follow PXDesign to rely on the in silico filter from AF2-IG, where a designable binder is defined as: a) interface predicted absolute error (ipAE) less than 10.85 A, and b) interface predicted TM score (ipTM) greater than 0.5, and c) predicted local distance difference test (pLDDT) greater than 80%, and d) binder bound/unbound RMSD less than 3.5 A. AF2 is used to evaluate these metrics, in which residues in the binder chain are assigned a large offset to mimic multichain co-folding. Across different binder lengths for the same target, the success counts are summed to obtain the final result.

target_definition_sources.citation: Zambaldi et al., De novo design of high-affinity protein binders with AlphaProteo, arXiv:2409.08022, Table S1 'Binder design problem specifications for in silico benchmarking and experimental testing. Input target structures and hotspot residues for the design targets addressed here.'
target_definition_sources.note: PRIMARY SOURCE for all ten targets. A-CODE says the test set is 'as proposed in Zambaldi et al.'; PXDesign says the same and that it 'adopted the cropping schemes and hotspot selections described in the respective original studies'. Table S1 gives PDB ID, target chain + residue numbers, hotspot residues and a per-target binder length range. Every entry below was re-verified against the local mmCIF mirror; see each target's `note`.

target_definition_sources.citation: PXDesign: Fast, Modular, and Accurate De Novo Design of Protein Binders (Protenix Team, ByteDance Seed), technical report v3 (2025-12-12), Table 3 'Targets and experimental results of PXDesign-d binders'.
target_definition_sources.note: CORROBORATING SOURCE for the six targets it lists. It agrees with AlphaProteo Table S1 character-for-character on SC2RBD, IL7RA, PDL1, TrkA and VEGFA (PDB, crop and hotspots), and on TNFa's crop. It DISAGREES on TNFa's hotspots -- see that target's note. Where they disagree, AlphaProteo wins, because that is the source A-CODE cites.

filter.name: AF2-IG
filter.equivalent_to: the 'AF2-IG-easy' row of PXDesign technical report Table 2, whose thresholds are BindCraft's: ipAE < 10.85, ipTM > 0.5, pLDDT > 0.8, binder bound/unbound RMSD < 3.5 A
filter.chain_break_offset_note: CHOSEN VALUE. The paper says only that binder-chain residues are 'assigned a large offset to mimic multichain co-folding' and gives no number; 200 is the AF2-multimer/AF2-IG convention. Override with --chain-break-offset if your AF2-IG wrapper uses a different one.

sampling.note: A-CODE states its own range explicitly -- 'lengths ranging from 80 to 130' -- and a per-target total of 328-728, with per-length success counts summed. It does not publish the per-length sample counts, so this ships a uniform 6-length x 64-sample = 384 grid, inside the paper's envelope. AlphaProteo's own per-target ranges are recorded per target as `alphaproteo_binder_length_range` for traceability; they are wider than A-CODE's window (40-140) and are deliberately NOT used to reshape the grid, since A-CODE overrides them with 80-130. Per-target `lengths` / `samples_per_length` overrides are honoured if you want to intersect them.
sampling.diffusion_steps_note: A-CODE Section 4.1: 'we follow PXDesign to use 1000 Euler steps for diffusion sampling'. PXDesign's own report used 400 steps for binder generation and 1000 for monomers; A-CODE states 1000 uniformly, so 1000 is the default here.

targets.name: BHRF1
targets.note: 157 cropped residues. All six hotspots resolve (PHE65, THR74, GLU77, ASP82, SER85, ARG93) and sit 3.3-7.1 A from the BH3 helix (chain B) in the deposited complex.

targets.name: H1
targets.note: NUMBERING OFFSET, the one place this manifest does not transcribe Table S1 literally. AlphaProteo writes the HA2 chain as 'B1-68, B80-170' with hotspots 'B21, B45, B52', i.e. canonical HA2 numbering 1-175; 5VLI deposits HA2 as author residues 501-670. Chain B is therefore stored here with +500 applied (ranges and hotspots alike) so it is author numbering like every other entry, while chain A (HA1) needs no shift. Confirmed: B521/B545/B552 resolve to TRP/ILE/VAL, each 3.5-3.8 A from a non-cropped chain -- the HA stem epitope. Without the shift all three hotspots are absent from the crop, which is how the offset was found. 280 cropped residues (chain A is observed from 5, so A1-50 intersects to A5-50).

targets.name: IL17A
targets.note: Both halves of the IL-17A dimer are the target (213 cropped residues). Hotspots resolve to GLN94/LEU116 on A and TRP67 on B, 2.8-3.7 A from IL-17RA in the deposited complex.

targets.name: IL7RA
targets.note: Crop is chain B's full observed range. Hotspots resolve to VAL58/LEU80/TYR139, 3.5-3.8 A from IL-7. PXDesign Table 3 lists this target identically.

targets.name: IR
targets.note: AlphaProteo labels this row 'Insulin' and A-CODE Table 4 calls it 'IR'; the specification is unambiguous either way. 4ZXB chain E is the 800-residue insulin-receptor ectodomain and E6-155 crops its L1 domain (150 residues). All three hotspots resolve to PHE -- PHE64/PHE88/PHE96, the documented L1 insulin-binding patch -- which is what pins the numbering. The interface distance check does not apply here: nothing else in the entry comes within 13 A of them, so no partner is bound at that site in this deposition (same situation as apo 1TNF).

targets.name: PDL1
targets.note: Hotspots are TYR56/MET115/TYR123, 2.2-2.9 A from the partner chain. Corroborated twice over: PXDesign Table 3 lists it identically, and PXDesign's shipped examples/PDL1_quick_start.yaml crops chain A to '1-116' with hotspots [40, 99, 107] in 1-based within-chain indexing -- 116 residues, and 17+40-1=56, 17+99-1=115, 17+107-1=123.

targets.name: SC2RBD
targets.note: Crop is chain E's full observed range. Hotspots are GLY485/TYR489/SER494/THR500/TYR505 on the ACE2-binding ridge, 2.7-6.2 A from ACE2 (chain A). PXDesign Table 3 lists this target identically.

targets.name: TNFa
targets.note: SOURCES DISAGREE HERE. AlphaProteo Table S1 gives two hotspots, A113 and C73; PXDesign Table 3 gives five, A31, A32, A113, C73, C87. The crop (the whole homotrimer, 438 residues) is identical in both. This manifest follows AlphaProteo, because A-CODE defines its test set as the targets 'proposed in Zambaldi et al.' and PXDesign's Table 3 is its own wet-lab campaign rather than the in-silico benchmark spec. Both listed residues resolve (PRO113 on A, HIS73 on C). 1TNF is apo, so the interface distance check does not apply.

targets.name: TrkA
targets.note: Crop is chain X's full observed range (the TrkA-d5 domain). Hotspots are VAL294/MET296/LEU333, 3.0-3.9 A from NGF. PXDesign Table 3 lists this target identically.

targets.name: VEGFA
targets.note: Both halves of the VEGF-A homodimer are the target (188 cropped residues); hotspots sit on chain W only. MET81/ILE83/ILE91, 3.2-3.8 A from the Fab in the deposited complex. PXDesign Table 3 lists this target identically.
